acceptance.given: Aggregate execution is run through the Toolchain aggregate evaluator with configured time and output bounds.

oracle.expected: Every terminating aggregate record contains a terminal state selected deterministically from the execution outcome; equivalent repeated runs yield the same terminal state and budget exhaustion is unsuccessful.
forbidden: An aggregate terminates without a terminal state.
An aggregate hangs beyond its configured bound.
Equivalent executions produce unexplained different terminal states.
oracle.observable: Aggregate evaluator output records and repeated-run comparison, including timeout and output-budget handling.

acceptance.then: The validator accepts only when every aggregate has a deterministic terminal state and rejects missing, hanging, or nondeterministic outcomes.
acceptance.when: After each aggregate execution terminates and during repeated deterministic replay.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the aggregate evaluator with a fixture exceeding the configured time or output budget; assert bounded termination with an unsuccessful terminal state.
Replay an equivalent aggregate execution twice with divergent terminal outcomes; assert the determinism check fails.

affected_subjects: aggregate terminal-state evaluation and deterministic replay
slice_hint.behavior_change: Record and validate a deterministic terminal state for every aggregate, including bounded unsuccessful termination on budget exhaustion and stable repeated-run results.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing aggregate result fields while adding deterministic terminal-state validation compatible with current replay records.

slice_hint.state_transition: aggregate executing -> bounded terminal state (success or unsuccessful budget-exhausted outcome)
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All aggregate records have a terminal state, no execution exceeds bounds, and equivalent executions produce the same terminal state.

acceptance.given: A repair or recompilation run has a pre-repair snapshot of historical tracked bytes and performs append-only evidence writes.

oracle.expected: Byte-for-byte comparison of every historical artifact before and after repair is identical; only append-only repair evidence may differ.
forbidden: Any historical file is rewritten, truncated, or corrupted.
The check compares only metadata or filenames instead of bytes.
oracle.observable: Validator comparison report containing pre-repair and post-repair byte hashes for each historical artifact.

acceptance.then: The validator passes only when all historical artifact bytes remain identical and fails on any byte mismatch.
acceptance.when: After repair or recompilation completes, before acceptance is published.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Mutate one byte in a historical tracked artifact in a controlled fixture, then run byte-integrity validation and require a mismatch failure.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate byte-for-byte preservation of historical artifacts across repair while permitting only append-only evidence additions.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain existing evidence validation inputs and add historical-byte comparison without rewriting stored artifacts.

slice_hint.state_transition: pre-repair historical bytes snapshotted -> post-repair byte comparison -> pass or integrity failure
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every historical artifact's post-repair bytes equal its pre-repair bytes; any mismatch is a terminal validation failure.

acceptance.given: Each Matrix Case is configured with Stable and Candidate executions and their case-specific fixture/state assignments.

oracle.expected: The per-case execution manifest contains two distinct fixture/state identities, one attributable to Stable and one to Candidate, for every Matrix Case.
forbidden: Stable and Candidate reference the same fixture/state identity where distinctness is required.
A Matrix Case omits either subject's fixture/state assignment.
oracle.observable: Parsed Matrix Case execution manifest and validator output showing distinct Stable and Candidate fixture-state identifiers per case.

acceptance.then: The validator passes only when all Matrix Cases have complete and distinct Stable/Candidate fixture/state assignments.
acceptance.when: During Matrix Case configuration validation, before subject execution is accepted.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use a Matrix Case manifest with identical Stable and Candidate fixture/state identifiers and assert the distinctness validator rejects it.
Use a Matrix Case manifest missing one subject assignment and assert completeness validation rejects it.

affected_subjects: Stable and Candidate per-case fixture/state assignment validation
slice_hint.behavior_change: Require and validate distinct, attributable fixture/state identities for Stable and Candidate in every Matrix Case.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep the existing Matrix Case manifest shape and add required distinct fixture/state identity checks.

slice_hint.state_transition: Matrix Case configured -> fixture/state identities validated -> subject execution eligible or rejected
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: For every Matrix Case, Stable and Candidate each have a fixture/state assignment and the two assignments are distinct.

acceptance.given: An actor attempts to publish an acceptance-passed result and the current Acceptance lifecycle owner is explicitly identified.

oracle.expected: Publication succeeds only for the current Acceptance lifecycle owner; every non-owner attempt is denied, and the authorization set is machine-verifiably empty for other actors.
forbidden: An actor other than the current Acceptance lifecycle owner is treated as authorized.
oracle.observable: Authorization validator result for owner and non-owner publication attempts, including the empty authorization-set artifact.

acceptance.then: The governance check passes only when owner authorization succeeds and all non-owner attempts are rejected.
acceptance.when: At acceptance publication authorization evaluation, before the acceptance-passed artifact is committed.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Invoke publication with a non-owner actor while the current Acceptance lifecycle owner is fixed; assert authorization denial and no acceptance-passed publication.
Provide a non-empty machine authorization set or owner identity mismatch in the publication artifact; assert governance validation rejects it.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce that only the current Acceptance lifecycle owner may publish acceptance-passed and expose an empty machine-verifiable authorization set for all other actors.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing governance policy interfaces and denial behavior while tightening publication-owner checks.

slice_hint.state_transition: publication attempt -> owner authorization decision -> published acceptance-passed or denied
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Exactly the current Acceptance lifecycle owner can publish acceptance-passed; all non-owner attempts are denied and the authorization set is empty for them.
